chunks: Al-Sakuni narrated with his chain of transmission; he said: Ali, peace be upon him, said:
The hand of Allah hovers with mercy above the head of the judge; but when he deviates in judgment, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, leaves him to himself.

key_terms.إِلَى نَفْسِهِ: to himself, meaning deprived of divine support
key_terms.الْحَاكِمِ: the judge or ruler entrusted with judgment
key_terms.بِالرَّحْمَةِ: with mercy, meaning divine compassion and support
key_terms.تُرَفْرِفُ: hovers or flutters above, indicating nearness and ongoing care
key_terms.حَافَ: deviated, acted unjustly, or inclined away from fairness
key_terms.يَدُ اللَّهِ: Allah’s hand; an expression here indicating divine care, aid, and mercy

ai.seo_question: What does Imam Ali عليه السلام say about Allah’s support for a judge who rules justly?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that divine mercy and aid accompany the ruler or judge so long as he judges justly. If he inclines toward injustice in judgment, Allah withdraws that support and leaves him to his own self.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3228 - Al-Sakuni narrated with his chain of transmission that Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) said:
"The hand of Allah (swt) hovers with mercy above the head of the judge. But if he deviates in judgment, Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, leaves him to himself."
